seo.title: DuckDB client for {devices}
seo.description: Open DuckDB files, query Parquet, CSV and JSON files where they sit, work in memory, and back up to a DuckDB file or Parquet with nothing to install.

header.title: DuckDB client
header.lead: Open a DuckDB database, or query Parquet, CSV and JSON files with SQL, with no database server to run.

bands.title: Open a file
text: Open a .duckdb or .ddb file, from Finder too, enter a new path to create one, or use :memory: for a temporary database. Files are identified by their header, not their extension.

Parquet, CSV, TSV, JSON and NDJSON open with File > Open File as read-only views named file and after the filename, and the source file is never changed. Remote (Quack, experimental) connects to a quack_serve server under an alias; the first connection downloads DuckDB’s quack extension.

bands.title: Query and edit
text: Query files directly, such as SELECT * FROM 'data.csv'. ATTACH adds another DuckDB file to the sidebar and ⌘K switches between them, until the next reconnect. EXPLAIN is drawn as a plan diagram.

Rows in a table can be edited, while the views over a data file stay read-only: create a table in a DuckDB database to edit its data. There is no create or drop database action; enter a new path when connecting to create a file.

bands.title: Share the file and back it up
text: While TablePro holds a file, the duckdb CLI, a notebook or a dbt run cannot open it. Release the File Lock After hands the file back after some idle minutes and takes it again on the next query, Open the File Read-Only lets several readers share it, and Database > Release File Lock hands it back at once. A release is refused, with the reason, while the session holds a transaction, a temporary table, an attached database or a changed setting.

Backup Dump needs nothing installed, because {dumpTool} writes it over the open connection: a .duckdb file to restore later, or a folder with schema.sql, load.sql and one Parquet file per table, which pandas, Spark and BigQuery read directly.

moveData: <importData>Import</importData> {importFormats} files, and export tables and results as {exportFormats}. The <export>Parquet export plugin</export>, from Settings > Plugins, adds Parquet output, one file per table.
iphone: DuckDB is part of the app there. A file you pick in the Files app opens where it is rather than as a copy, In-Memory gives a scratch database, and you browse tables as cards and run SQL in the Query tab.

faq.question: Which DuckDB version does TablePro use?
faq.answer: DuckDB {engineVersion}, compiled into the driver. It does not depend on any DuckDB you have installed.

faq.question: Should I open a CSV file in DuckDB or in the Data Files window?
faq.answer: Use the <dataFiles>Data Files window</dataFiles> to look through a file, clean it up and save it back. Open it as DuckDB to join it with other files or tables in SQL; the file stays read-only there.
